reports.summary: Historical ES NQ GC rejection paths, cloud comparisons and a separate assumed-cost 3R policy. Final evaluation 2024–2025 with distinct development, validation, recent replication and earlier robustness; input and execution limitations remain explicit.
reports.title: Camarilla reversals and the EMA20/50 cloud

reports.summary: An external evidence study and proposed first-touch VAH/VAL-to-POC strategy. Two overlapping snapshots, seven source charts, reported rates and sample counts, contrary evidence, execution gaps and a plan for future independent Abacus analysis.
reports.title: Value-area fade tracker: 55 to 100 reported trades

reports.summary: Saved GC excursion means, coverage and horizon-specific evidence at a ten-bar cooldown. Annual regimes differ; MAE/MFE extrema and terminal rates do not establish executable profits.
reports.title: GC EMA outer band: years, cohorts and path scale

reports.summary: Saved two-sigma departure and first-touch evidence at 20 and 100 minutes, separated by product and anchor. Each horizon has its own complete-path denominator; return, endpoint and barrier-first outcomes answer different questions.
reports.title: VWAP excursions: separate sessions, horizons and first-move outcomes

reports.summary: Bar-colour continuation is common in the saved FX exports, but added lead-up does not show supported primary prediction improvement. Strict three-bar price paths and uncertainty have separate denominators and units.
reports.title: Range XV reversals: persistence, prediction and price are separate

reports.summary: A qualitative review of Tmac's weekly-to-intraday decision process, with selected charts showing confirmation, a no-trade day, reassessment and an unmet target. One reviewed week does not establish independently verified performance or profitability.
reports.title: NQ advanced AMD: bias, confirmation and abstention

reports.summary: The retained historical comparison does not establish a clear ES or NQ chart winner. Requested GC 20 evidence is missing; chart identity and timing remain provisional.
reports.title: Reversal follow-through: no clear chart winner

reports.summary: Saved candle geometry estimates condition on eventual same-direction closes. Corrected complete-leg duration is a raw clock proxy; neither result is a live entry filter.
reports.title: Follow-through candle: conditional adverse movement

reports.summary: Strictly prior larger-chart alignment improves next-bar colour continuation most consistently in ES and GC. Longer runs are less stable; shared price streams limit independence.
reports.title: Chart alignment: stronger next-bar persistence

reports.summary: Aligned strong candles show a next-bar colour advantage that weakens over longer runs. Saved mean next-bar returns remain negative before costs, despite high continuation rates.
reports.title: Reversal quality: colour advantage, negative payoff

reports.summary: Persistent states retain more future residence, while opposing slopes predict more crossing. Coarse matching shrinks both gaps; local-anchor checks reverse the pooled VWAP–TWAP conclusion.
reports.title: VWAP states: persistence, slope conflict and fair-price error

reports.summary: Three ES/NQ/GC chart-price candidates fail the frozen cost and familywise screen. Retrospectively inspected dates and unverified completion/fill timing limit trading claims.
reports.title: Range XV: three candidates fail the declared screen

reports.summary: Across seven ES/GC/NQ Range XV settings, the frozen two-more-bar screen finds no supported positive rate above fifty percent. Chart colour continuation is descriptive, not a payoff test.
reports.title: Countertrend reversals: bar persistence is not an edge

reports.summary: Across seven ES/GC/NQ Range XV settings, the frozen two-more-bar screen finds no supported positive lift above its chart/direction/window baseline. Chart colour continuation is descriptive, not a payoff test.
reports.title: Countertrend reversals: bar persistence is not an edge

reports.summary: Some confirmed cohorts beat ordinary two-bar baselines, but waiting does not improve signed chart-price means. Confirmed samples and original opportunities have different denominators.
reports.title: Second-candle confirmation: colour lift and price disagree

reports.summary: Asia, London and New York overlays preserve negative price screens. Selected NQ colour contrasts vary by session, while the confirmation wait policy remains negative.
reports.title: Session overlay: local colour patterns do not prove edge

reports.summary: Asia, London and New York overlays preserve negative price screens. Selected NQ colour contrasts vary by session, while the confirmation wait policy remains negative.
reports.title: Session overlay: local colour patterns do not prove edge

reports.summary: Conditional checkpoint and destination probabilities describe mature VWAP episodes. Geometry adds only small context-model improvements; these are exploratory associations, not trading probabilities.
reports.title: VWAP checkpoints: return, extension and destination probabilities

reports.summary: Next-open GC excursions after a close below the outer lower EMA band vary by year. The saved default grid is descriptive; excursion extrema are not executable exits.
reports.title: GC outer lower band: yearly excursion paths

reports.summary: An upper-half signal close was selected in 2025. Its chronological 2026 improvement remains uncertain, and the filtered score is negative; this is conditional path evidence.
reports.title: GC lower band: filter improvement remains uncertain

reports.summary: The original A–C protocol studies POC reversal, value-boundary retest and pre-touch HVN fade on NQ. Matched-control evidence is mixed; later D/E extensions are excluded.
reports.title: Asia volume-profile levels: the original three setups

reports.summary: Fresh two-sigma departures show different return and response behavior by anchor and product. Complete-path denominators and shared-week uncertainty limit these to exploratory price evidence.
reports.title: VWAP excursion: return and first-touch response

reports.summary: Eight FX chart/direction populations retain separate continuation rates. Adding prior-leg length or richer history yields no supported primary log-loss improvement beyond reversal geometry and context.
reports.title: FX Range XV: lead-up adds no supported primary prediction

reports.summary: A qualitative review of Tmac's weekly-to-intraday decision process, with selected charts showing confirmation, a no-trade day, reassessment and an unmet target. One reviewed week does not establish independently verified performance or profitability.
reports.title: NQ advanced AMD: bias, confirmation and abstention

reports.summary: ES, NQ and GC price-path evidence shows frequent return by window end, while extreme fades and first retest bounces do not demonstrate stable incremental advantage. These observations do not establish net profitability.
reports.title: Session VWAP: returns, fades and first retests
